lamejs -- MP3 encoder, vendored unmodified as static/vendor/lamejs.js

Upstream:  https://github.com/zhuker/lamejs  (npm lamejs 1.2.1)
Declared:  LGPL-3.0  (package.json)
Derived from LAME:  https://lame.sourceforge.net

Full licence text accompanies this file as LGPL-3.0.txt, together with
GPL-3.0.txt, which the LGPL incorporates by reference.

The file vendored here is lame.all.js, the unminified build. lame.min.js
exists and is smaller, but the LGPL asks for the form preferred for making
modifications, and it is loaded only when an export runs.

--- upstream LICENSE, verbatim ---

Can I use LAME in my commercial program?  

Yes, you can, under the restrictions of the LGPL.  The easiest
way to do this is to:

1. Link to LAME as separate jar (lame.min.js or lame.all.js)

2. Fully acknowledge that you are using LAME, and give a link
   to our web site, lame.sourceforge.net

3. If you make modifications to LAME, you *must* release these
   these modifications back to the LAME project, under the LGPL.
